title: They weren’t the kind of men you build movements with.
paragraphs: They weren’t the kind of men you build movements with.

Not polished.
Not platform-ready.
Not “anointed-looking.”

They were tired.
Calloused.
Complicated.

One smelled like fish and failure.
Another carried the weight of betrayal in his pockets.
One burned with political rage.
Another hid behind questions he couldn’t silence.
And Jesus… walked straight past the religious elites.

He didn’t recruit from the temples.
He didn’t consult the scholars.
He didn’t assemble a panel of the already-approved.
He stepped into the dust, into the ordinary, into the overlooked—and He called them.
“Follow Me.” (Matthew 4:19)
That’s it.

No résumé.
No background check.
No spiritual interview.
Just a command wrapped in grace.
But don’t miss this…

Jesus didn’t call them because they were ready.
He called them knowing they weren’t.

Peter would open his mouth too fast—and later deny Him three times (Luke 22:61).
Matthew had built a life profiting off his own people (Luke 5:27–32).
Thomas would demand proof when faith felt too fragile (John 20:25).
Judas… would walk close to Jesus and still choose betrayal (Matthew 26:14–16).
This wasn’t a team of perfect men.
This was a gallery of broken stories.
And still—He chose them.
Why?
Because the Kingdom of God isn’t built on human strength.
It’s built on surrendered hearts.
“God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong.” (1 Corinthians 1:27)
Let that sit.
God didn’t make a mistake when He called the unqualified.
He made a statement.

That salvation doesn’t belong to the impressive.
That grace doesn’t flow to the deserving.
That transformation begins where pride ends.
But here’s where it gets personal…
Some of you are still disqualifying yourselves.

Because of your past.
Because of that secret struggle.
Because of the version of you that still haunts your quiet moments.
You think:

“I’m too far gone.”
“I’ve messed up too much.”
“I’m not like them.”
But look again at the men Jesus called.
They were “too much” too.

Too impulsive.
Too corrupt.
Too doubtful.
Too broken.
And still—He said, “Follow Me.”
Listen carefully:
Jesus does not call the worthy.
He makes worthy the called.
That’s the Gospel.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” (Ephesians 2:8)
A gift.

Not a reward.
Not a transaction.
Not something you earn after cleaning yourself up.
Because if you could fix yourself, you wouldn’t need a Savior.
And that’s where the cross speaks louder than your past.

At the cross, your sin is not minimized—it is paid for.
At the cross, your shame is not ignored—it is covered.
At the cross, your failure is not the end—it is the place where grace begins.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
While.

Not after you improved.
Not when you got your life together.
While you were still in it.
That’s how deep His love runs.
And then comes the resurrection.
Because Jesus didn’t just call broken men—He raised them into bold witnesses.

Peter, who denied Him, would stand and preach—and thousands would be saved (Acts 2:14, 41).
Thomas, who doubted, would declare, “My Lord and my God!” (John 20:28).
Matthew, once greedy, would write the Gospel that still changes lives today.
This is what Jesus does.
He doesn’t just call you out of something.
He calls you into someone new.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” (2 Corinthians 5:17)
So the question is not:
“Are you qualified?”
The question is:
Will you follow?

Will you lay down the old identity?
Will you surrender the hidden sin?
Will you trust that His grace is stronger than your history?
Because right now—yes, right now—Jesus is still calling.
Not the perfect.
Not the polished.
But the willing.
And maybe that’s you.

If your heart is beating a little heavier reading this…
If something inside you is saying, “This is for me…”
Don’t ignore that.
That’s not guilt.
That’s invitation.
Turn to Him.

Repent.
Believe.
Follow.
And watch what grace can do with a life that says yes to Jesus.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
